nus_desc: Introduction to financial accounting. Covers accounting equations, financial statements, and interpreting corporate annual reports.
Basic economic principles applied to business. Focuses on consumer behavior, market structures, and pricing strategies.
Study of common materials used in civil engineering. Covers properties of steel, concrete, timber, and sustainable building materials.
Fundamentals of electronics. Covers semiconductor physics, diodes, bipolar junction transistors, and operational amplifiers.
Foundational data literacy. Covers statistical sampling, visualization, probability, and making inferences from real-world data.
Historical and sociological study of Singapore’s development. Analyzes national identity, urban planning, and social policies.
Core calculus for engineering students. Includes differential equations, partial derivatives, and multiple integrals.
Theory and application of first and second-order differential equations and Laplace transforms.
Mechanical engineering core. Analyzes stress, strain, torsion, and bending of beams in structural components.
Structure of materials at the atomic level. Discusses mechanical, electrical, and thermal properties of metals and polymers.
Professional practice in healthcare. Covers therapeutic interventions, patient assessment, and ethical clinical reasoning.
Foundational philosophical questions. Explores ethics, epistemology, and the nature of reality through classic texts.
Fundamental concepts of problem solving by computing. Includes variables, control structures, functions, and arrays.
Object-oriented programming and functional programming paradigms using Java. Covers inheritance, polymorphism, and generics.
Focuses on data structure design and complexity analysis. Covers heaps, balanced search trees, and graph algorithms.
Understanding computer systems from logic gates to instruction sets. Covers MIPS architecture, pipelining, and cache memory.
Relational database design and implementation. Focuses on SQL, relational algebra, and normalization theory.
Principles of large-scale software development. Covers design patterns, unit testing, and version control using Git.
Fundamental concepts in networking. Includes protocol layers, TCP/UDP, socket programming, and network security.
Concepts of OS design including process management, CPU scheduling, memory management, and file systems.
Advanced algorithm design techniques including dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, and NP-completeness.
Fundamentals of 3D rendering, including transformations, lighting models, texture mapping, and ray tracing.
Core AI concepts including heuristic search, constraint satisfaction, logic-based agents, and probability.
Introduction to supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, decision trees, and model evaluation.
Calculus concepts for computer science, including limits, derivatives, integration, and series expansions.
Systems of linear equations, vector spaces, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors with applications in computing.
Probability theory and statistical inference for engineers. Covers random variables, distributions, and hypothesis testing.
Focuses on oral and written communication skills specifically for computing and technical environments.
